body:
> but I didn't get past the syntax validation (type cannot be null).

Looking at the code, it seems like this would only occur when serializing to another node. I actually don't immediately see where we validate that `type` shouldn't be `null`. 

When you say you got "syntax validation" could you post what failure you did receive @demjened?

I used the example parent ID mapping and request in the [documentation](https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/query-dsl-parent-id-query.html#query-dsl-parent-id-query) without a `type` attribute.

I just tested it again on a 8.12.0 deployment, and I saw some race condition-like anomaly. Executing the query many times in a row resulted randomly in either
- 400 with an error message `[parent_id] no relation found for child [null]`
- 500 with the `Cannot invoke \"String.length()\" because \"str\" is null\"` error message


https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/assets/14224983/6ba10f52-3aa2-4a2e-ae65-329619b84033
thank you @demjened , The bug fix isn't too bad. Looks like @original-brownbear has taken up the cause.

We need to enforce non-null values here, otherwise we'll error out and return a 500 when a user fails to set either id or type.

closes #105366
